title: East St. Louis Toodle-oo as theme and the Cotton Club radio broadcasts
summary: Greer remembers the first theme song, chimes under growling brass, and the nightly broadcasts with announcers Ted Husing and others.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Because our first theme song was -- what the hell is the name of that thing, the prettiest one, long before "A-Train." That was the prettiest, "East St. Louis Toodle-oo." Bubber Miley named it that. That was the prettiest theme song we ever had. "A-Train," with all due respect, couldn't even play in the same place with it. We had -- I played chimes all the way through, cathedral chimes and the band was low down growling, real low down, low, low, way down near the bottom. So.... Jungle music.

When we stopped playing that for our theme song, that thing broke my heart. That was the prettiest thing and we used to play it. We broadcast -- we used to broadcast from the Cotton Club from 6:00 to 7:00, every night. We had three of the best announcers. We had Ted Husing, Dick Brokenshire

and David (unintelligible). Three of the best announcers in the business, in the world. They would come up to the Cotton Club especially Ted Husing, he's still living. Like you make out a program, you know, different numbers you want to play. He wouldn't let us. He would say you play this, and he would pick out some of our finest. That's right.
